summary: Iberian Gauge is a fast, lighter cousin of 18xx train games: you alternate buying stock in rail companies with operating rounds where your shares (in purchase order) let you extend that company's network across a hex map of Iberia, leasing rival track to save money. It plays in well under two hours but keeps the genre's core tension of propping up a company's stock price through expansion versus personally profiting from dividends and cash.
praised: Much faster and more approachable than full 18xx while keeping real economic tension
The share-purchase-order-determines-build-order mechanic creates clever, tight decision points
Leasing track from other companies is an elegant cost-saving twist
Good table presence and production for a small-press game
criticised: Turn order and initial company assignment can create swingy, luck-influenced starts
Rules have some ambiguous edge cases around leasing and connections
Smaller map can feel cramped with more players, limiting expansion options
Stock round downtime while waiting for others to act

interaction.kind: network blocking and route competition intertwined with stock manipulation

scoring.why: The winner is whoever ends with the most combined cash and stock value, driven almost entirely by how well their companies' networks and dividends performed
